slides.title: From First Chechen War to War of Dagestan
slides.cap: Historical connection: Chechen conflict spreads into Dagestan
slides.body: The unresolved First Chechen War left armed Islamist factions operating from Chechnya. Their invasion of neighboring Dagestan attempted to spread rebellion across the North Caucasus.

slides.title: Before the War of Dagestan
slides.body: Islamist fighters based in Chechnya entered Dagestan hoping to trigger an uprising and establish a broader Islamic state.

stats.val: The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

slides.cap: Historical connection: Chechen conflict spreads into Dagestan

markers.label: Karamakhi
markers.description: Karamakhi was one of the fortified militant villages retaken by federal forces.

slides.title: Battle of Karamakhi
slides.body:
The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

Consequences: The effects of Battle of Karamakhi extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

Karamakhi and nearby Chabanmakhi had become fortified centers for Islamist militants who rejected Dagestan's secular authorities. Federal forces used artillery, armor, and house-to-house fighting to retake the area. The battle mattered because it showed Moscow that the Dagestan incursion was not only a border raid from Chechnya, but also had local strongpoints that had to be reduced village by village.

stats.lbl: Federal forces began bombarding the fortified Karamakhi area in late August 1999; militants withdrew by 13 September and the villages were left ruined.

markers.description: Botlikh marks the district attacked by militants entering Dagestan from Chechnya.

slides.title: Tsumadinsky-Botlikhsky campaign
slides.body:
The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

Consequences: The effects of Tsumadinsky-Botlikhsky campaign extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

stats.lbl: On 7 August 1999, roughly 1,500–2,000 militants invaded Dagestan and seized villages in the Tsumadi and Botlikh districts.

markers.description: This height dominated local routes and became a costly tactical fight.

slides.title: Battle for Donkey's Ear Height
slides.body:
The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

Consequences: The effects of Battle for Donkey's Ear Height extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

stats.lbl: The August 1999 fighting for the strategic Donkey's Ear height involved federal paratroopers and Islamist militants; one six-hour battle killed 12 paratroopers and wounded 25.

markers.label: Height 715.3
markers.description: Height 715.3 is marked because militants captured it before federal counterattacks.

slides.title: Wahhabi capture of Height 715,3
slides.body:
The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

Consequences: The effects of Wahhabi capture of Height 715,3 extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

stats.lbl: Militants captured Height 715.3 on 5–6 September 1999; up to 50 militants were killed or wounded in the fighting.

markers.label: Tukhchar
markers.description: Tukhchar marks the massacre site where captured Russian soldiers were executed.

slides.title: Tukhchar massacre
slides.body: The Tukhchar massacre was an incident during the War in Dagestan which was filmed and distributed on tape, in which Russian prisoners of war were executed. Throughout the battle, Russian soldiers reported finding taped executions of Russian officers and men. Some videos were later sold as snuff films and ended up being posted online. One tape created in September 1999 showed six Russian servicemen, five as young as 19, who were conscripts, being executed by Chechen and Dagestani militants. The method was piercing the trachea, also known as beheading.

stats.lbl: The Tukhchar massacre was an incident during the War in Dagestan which was filmed and distributed on tape, in which Russian prisoners of war were executed.

slides.title: Consequences
slides.body: The effects of Tukhchar massacre extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

slides.body:
Foreign fighters joined the militants, but the campaign remained primarily a Russian and Dagestani response.

slides.title: The End of the War of Dagestan
slides.body: Russian forces and local Dagestani militias expelled the attackers. The crisis became the immediate prelude to the Second Chechen War.
